name: Meridian Munitions Compact-7 'Rat Trap'
description:
The Meridian Munitions Compact-7 is a subcompact pistol designed for deep concealment, chambered in .32 ACP. The frame is a single-piece carbon composite that flexes slightly under recoil — a design feature Meridian markets as 'recoil absorption' but which shooters recognize as structural cheapness. The slide is thin stamped steel with a matte black coating that chips within weeks of regular carry.

The Rat Trap fills the niche between the absolute bottom-shelf disposables and actual defensive firearms. It is marginally more accurate than a Payday, marginally more reliable, and marginally more expensive. Office workers in lower-Mid districts carry them in ankle holsters and purse compartments, telling themselves it provides real protection.

Meridian Munitions sells more Compact-7s than any other single firearm model in the lower Mids. The weapon has become so associated with anxious middle-tier workers that carrying one is sometimes used as shorthand for someone who is afraid but not afraid enough to spend real money on safety.
specifications:
caliber: .32 ACP
effective_range: 10 meters
rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic
magazine_capacity: 6 rounds
weight: 0.34 kg
tactical_use: Deep concealment weapon for close-range self-defense. The .32 ACP round lacks stopping power against armored or augmented targets. Effective only against unarmored soft targets at point-blank range. Tactical instructors generally advise emptying the magazine and running.
cultural_context: The Rat Trap is the butt of jokes in firearms circles and the quiet comfort of millions of lower-Mid workers who slip one into their coat pocket every morning. Its cultural position is one of quiet, slightly embarrassing pragmatism.
story_hooks: A corporate accountant pulls a Rat Trap during an office hostage situation — and it jams on the first round.
Thousands of Compact-7s are being recalled due to a firing pin defect, but someone is buying up the recalled units.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Galvanic Resuscitation Frame — 'The Pallbearer's Daughter'

physical_description.visual_profile: A diminutive, almost toy-like pistol with a blunt profile and minimal visual aggression. The compact silhouette screams 'ankle holster special' — something designed to disappear rather than intimidate. Its proportions are slightly stubby, lacking the sleek lines of higher-tier firearms.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 16.5 cm, Width: 3.2 cm, Height: 10.8 cm, Barrel length: 6.1 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Feels hollow in the hand — light but not elegant, more like holding a scaled-down toy than a serious implement. The flex in the composite frame is immediately noticeable when gripped firmly.
physical_description.primary_material: Single-piece carbon composite frame with stamped steel slide; plastic trigger guard
physical_description.finish: Matte black coating on slide with visible stress fractures and edge wear; dull charcoal composite frame with slight waffle-textured molding marks
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black slide with charcoal gray composite frame; small brushed steel breech face visible
physical_description.grip_texture: Cheap molded polymer with shallow grip serrations that feel more cosmetic than functional; slightly tacky to the touch
distinctive_features: Thin, flimsy-looking slide with pronounced flex when pressed
Minimalist sights — almost more etched than raised
Visible chipping on slide edges where black coating is wearing through to bare steel
Frame shows faint factory mold lines
Oversized trigger guard relative to trigger size
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small 'MERIDIAN MUNITIONS' stamp on left slide side, barely legible; tiny caliber marking '.32 ACP' near breech; generic serial number stamped directly into frame with visible imperfections
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn within weeks — edge-chipped slide finish, loose-feeling frame with micro-movements, trigger slightly scratchy from lint accumulation, magazines showing spring fatigue from repeated loading cycles
